Q: Can you describe a time you had to manage conflict within a team?
A: Yes, during my time as Lead Frontend Engineer at EriksDigital. The hardest challenge wasn't the code, but managing 'emotional debates' within the team. I had to step in, refine opinions, and steer conversations back to actionable next steps. It often meant proving to the delivery team that a solution simply wasn't ready, prioritizing honesty over pride to ensure we didn't ship bad code.

Q: What is your biggest professional achievement in terms of business revenue?
A: At A-Dam, I took over the development of their web-shop. I migrated the stack to NextJS to handle SEO and performance better. The result was that with Server-Side Rendering (SSR), page loads became 5x faster. This directly correlated to an increase in yearly revenue by over 100% and improved client retention by 75%.

Q: Why did you leave your last role at Hexaware/Mobiquity?
A: It was a result of corporate restructuring. After Mobiquity was acquired and migrated under Hexaware control, most projects were moved to the India office. I ended up working on bench projects because there were no projects left for the Dutch office. I was asked to resign with compensation, so I left in December 2025 to focus on upskilling.

Q: Your background starts in retail. How does that translate to software engineering?
A: I spent 5 years in retail sales in Ukraine, starting as a salesman collecting orders for basics like sunflower oil and noodles, and eventually becoming an Area Sales Manager for Nestle and Purina. It taught me how to negotiate with emotional partners who care only about revenue, not technical details. I learned to understand business needs first and build proposals that help them grow. That soft skill is crucial when I'm defining requirements for software.

Q: How do you handle difficult personnel decisions?
A: I believe in honesty. I once had a developer whose performance was low because he was unhappy with the growing requirements. We had a hard conversation where I shared my own story of leaving my first sales job to move into the unknown. I suggested he might be happier elsewhere. He actually returned to his previous profession in perfumery and lab work, and later I heard he was much happier and working without pressure.

Q: Why did you leave A-Dam if the project was so successful?
A: The web-shop was working perfectly, and the company shifted focus entirely to marketing rather than feature development. But the main reason was personal—I needed a permanent contract to apply for a Dutch mortgage to buy a house, and A-Dam couldn't provide that at the time.

Q: How do you handle high-pressure environments?
A: I learned this lesson the hard way. Early in my career, I worked in a harsh environment where I felt I had to work 18 hours a day to not 'fail' my colleagues. I was exhausted. From that, I learned the value of mental health and sustainable working paces. Now, I focus on planning and clear communication to avoid 'crunch' modes, ensuring I stay productive and positive for the long term.

Q: What is your core philosophy when it comes to professional development?
A: My philosophy is 'honesty over pride.' I value transparent communication and admitting mistakes because that is the only way to truly improve skills. I learned this early on in retail—hiding a problem never solves it, but addressing it head-on builds trust and leads to faster growth.

Q: Why did you leave DigitalChefs if you liked the startup environment?
A: I really enjoyed the work and the team's dedication, but I had a strict requirement regarding my visa. To secure uninterrupted work experience in the Netherlands for my residence permit—I need 5 years—I had to switch from my partner's visa to my own highly-skilled migrant visa. DigitalChefs wasn't able to provide that sponsorship at the time.

Q: Tell me about your time in retail before IT. What did you learn?
A: I worked as an Area Sales Manager for Nestle and Purina in the Stryj region, specifically with brands like Torchin and Mivina. It taught me how different people express concerns and fears. I learned to negotiate with partners who were extremely emotional and focused solely on revenue. That experience helps me now when I need to understand the business value behind a software requirement.

Q: Why did you choose to join Hexaware/Mobiquity?
A: I wanted to work in a service company to gain more experience in leadership and collaboration with Project Owners. I knew they invested heavily in engineer growth. My girlfriend had worked there for three years, so I knew they only hired very experienced developers who were ready to support each other. It felt like the right place to expand my T-shaped skills.

A: My mission is to deeply understand business requirements before touching the code. At Hexaware, I worked closely with Project Owners to ensure our Agentic Chat UI wasn't just technically sound, but optimized workflows for the users. I bridge the gap between business revenue goals and engineering, a skill I honed during my five years in retail sales.
